info.title: Logweir product API
info.description: The bounded shared-console product API (PLAT-17.1). Not a Kubernetes proxy: no generic resource path, no Secret, Pod, log, exec or Job access, no delete, and no arbitrary patch. Every error is application/problem+json. Unsafe methods require Content-Type: application/json and an Origin equal to the configured public origin. Durable creates require Idempotency-Key. Capabilities without a route are advertised false in /api/v1/session.

get.summary: The normalized status of one Backup, Restore, TopicDiscovery or Preflight. For a backup or a restore the body is an OperationResponse: result and evidence verification are separate, and NotAttempted is never verified success. For a discovery or a preflight it is a CheckOperationResponse, which carries none of those fields because a transient check has none of those facts.

parameters.description: An explicitly granted namespace. An ungranted namespace is namespace_forbidden whether or not it exists.

parameters.description: backup, restore, discovery or preflight.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The object name.

200.description: The normalized durable run (backup, restore), or the normalized transient check (discovery, preflight) — two shapes, because a check has no archive result, no signed evidence and no verification verdict.

default.description: An application/problem+json error; the possible codes are listed in x-logweir-problem-codes.

AccessGrantView.description: One role's grant, as stored. NEVER A CREDENTIAL VALUE: a Secret name and the key names inside it, both of which are public references.

keys.description: The data KEY NAMES inside it, sorted.

AccessModeDto.description: How one role's credential is obtained.

oneOf.description: Keys read from a Secret in this namespace, projected into the Job.
The pod's own ServiceAccount identity; no Secret is projected.
The controller's own read-only object-store handle. `evidenceRead` only.
The destination's explicit read-only `archiveRead` grant. `evidenceRead` only.

RESPONSES ONLY: the grant is absent and `archiveWrite` is used. It is never accepted in a request, because "absent" and "explicitly say the thing absence means" would then be two spellings of one state.
RESPONSES ONLY: `evidenceRead` is absent, so verification is `NotAttempted` and this says so rather than leaving a blank field.

AccessRequest.description: The four grants. Absent is a DEFINED answer and never a wider one: `archiveRead` and `evidenceWrite` absent mean "use `archiveWrite`", and `evidenceRead` absent means verification is not attempted and says so.

archiveWrite.description: The grant execution Jobs write the archive with. Required.

evidenceRead.description: The grant that reads evidence back for verification.

evidenceWrite.description: The grant that writes evidence under `logweir/`.

displayName.description: A display name. Never used for authorization.

AddressingDto.description:
How a request names the bucket.

NEVER A TRANSPORT CHOICE, in either direction. Addressing says how the bucket appears in the URL; `transport.security` alone decides whether the connection is encrypted. This is defect G5 written into the contract.

oneOf.description: `https://endpoint/bucket/key`.
`https://bucket.endpoint/key`.

Approval.description: Public approval metadata. The documents themselves are only on the packet route.

approvalBytesLength.description: The approval document's length in bytes.

approver.description: The approver subject from the roster.

matchedKeyId.description: The approver key that verified it.

planHash.description: The plan hash the create form supplied.

selfAttestedRisk.description: Whether approver and requester may be the same principal.

ticket.description: The change ticket the document names.

verified.description: Whether the controller verified the approval.

planHash.description: The plan hash the create form supplied.

replayed.description: On a durable create: whether this response replays an earlier identical request (HTTP 200) rather than creating (HTTP 201).

ArchiveRequest.description: An archive location in a request.

credentialRef.description: An existing Secret in this namespace carrying the object-store credential.

ArchiveView.description: An archive location and the name of the Secret that reaches it.

credentialRef.description: The name of the Secret carrying the object-store credential. A name only; this service never reads Secrets.

url.description: The object-store URL, with any userinfo redacted.

AuthenticationMode.description: How the current actor was authenticated.

oneOf.description: The explicit loopback administrator mode.
A validated OpenID Connect session.

observedAuth.description: The identity the run presented: mode and username, never a password.

schedule.description: The schedule that created the run.

windowCovered.description: The covered window, epoch milliseconds, end exclusive.

BackupPreflightRequest.description: The backup half of a preflight request.

schedule.description: The schedule this readiness is about, for context.

sourceConnection.description: The source connection, in this namespace.

replayed.description: On a durable create: whether this response replays an earlier identical request (HTTP 200) rather than creating (HTTP 201).

CaBundleRequest.description: A CA bundle in a `ConfigMap` in this namespace. A `ConfigMap` and never a Secret: a CA certificate is public material.

key.description: The data key holding the PEM bundle. Absent means `ca.crt`.

CaBundleView.description: A CA bundle reference, with the digest the controller observed.

sha256.description: `sha256:<hex>` over the CA bytes the controller read, so a rotation is visible without reading the bundle again.

CancelResponse.description:
`POST .../topic-discoveries/{id}:cancel` and `POST .../preflights/{id}:cancel`.

CANCELLATION IS A WISH, RECORDED. It never deletes archive data, Kafka topics, durable runs or signed evidence; the controller verifies the exact owned Job and UID before stopping anything.

alreadyTerminal.description: True when the check had already finished, in which case nothing was written. Repeating a cancel is 200 either way.

Capabilities.description:
The capability flags of one namespace grant.

Every flag is `implemented && allowed`. The eight domains that have no route in this build are always `false`.

credentialWrite.description: Write-only credential input: `POST .../destinations` and `:update-access` accept a credential value that is created once and never read back.

destinations.description: The saved-destination domain (PLAT-08) is served AND readable here.

preflight.description: The preflight domain (PLAT-03) is served AND readable here.

topicDiscovery.description:
The topic-discovery domain (PLAT-09.1) is served AND readable here.

ONE FLAG PER DOMAIN, AND IT IS THE READ FLOOR. D2 §8 names exactly three flags — `destinations`, `topicDiscovery`, `preflight` — so a domain gets one bit, not a bit per verb, and the bit answers "is this domain served and visible to me". Whether the actor may also START or CANCEL is the role table above, which `/session` publishes per grant in `roles`; a console reads `roles.includes("operator")` for the buttons and this flag for the page. Splitting these into read/start pairs is a contract change that must land together with `ui/contract.js`'s `CAPABILITY_FLAGS`.

CheckGating.description: Whether a check's verdict gates the operation.

oneOf.description: A `notReady` here makes the whole operation `notReady`.
Reported as a warning; never changes the aggregate.
Cannot be checked before execution; always `unknown` and always excluded from the aggregate.

CheckLifecycle.description: The lifecycle of a transient check.

oneOf.description: Accepted; the controller has not observed it yet.
Waiting for a check slot.
The check Job exists and has not finished.
A result was produced.
No result could be produced. Distinct from a result that says "no".
Cancelled before a result.
A phase this build does not recognise.

CheckOperation.description: The normalized status of one transient check.

cancellable.description: Whether this check may still be cancelled.

resourceVersion.description: The resourceVersion this status was read at.

CheckOperationKind.description:
The two transient check kinds with a status route.

SEPARATE FROM [`OperationKind`] ON PURPOSE. A check has no archive result, no signed evidence and no verification verdict, so folding it into [`Operation`] would mean publishing three fields that are meaningless for it and inviting a console to render "verification: pending" for a topic list.

oneOf.description: A `TopicDiscovery`.
A `Preflight`.
The check passed.

StaleReasonKind.description:
Why a stored readiness verdict no longer describes the caller's inputs.

CLOSED OVER EXACTLY WHAT THE CONTROLLER EMITS. These are the six spellings `logweir_core::check_contract::StaleReason` renders, and `crates/logweir-api/tests/preflights.rs` pins the two lists against each other so neither side can grow a reason the other cannot carry. A DTO that could not name `referentChanged` left W13 parsing the controller's prose to find out which object moved.

`cancelRequested` is DELIBERATELY ABSENT, and was in the first cut of this enum. The controller never emits it: a cancelled check is `state: cancelled` and carries no result at all, so its verdict is not stale — it is ABSENT, which is a different thing and one `state` and `terminal` already say. Reporting it here invited a console to render "your readiness result is out of date" for a check that never produced one.

oneOf.description: The verdict is past `expiresAt`, or recorded no expiry at all.
The plan the caller is looking at is not the plan the check was bound to.

A named object's UID or generation moved, or it appeared or vanished, since the verdict was computed — a recreated destination, an edited access block, a re-created recovery point, a `TrustRoster` edit, or an `Approval` whose resourceVersion moved when verification landed. [`StaleReasonView::kind`] and [`StaleReasonView::name`] say which.
A destination's CA bundle `ConfigMap` now digests differently, so the trust material the check exercised is not the trust material a run would use.

The installation policy `ConfigMap` digests differently, which can change the concurrency ceilings, the engine CA rule, the `ControllerIdentity` allowlist and the visibility attestations the verdict was computed under.

The recomputed inputs digest differs and none of the named reasons explains it. THE CATCH-ALL EXISTS SO "stale" IS NEVER REPORTED WITHOUT A REASON: a field the five named comparisons do not cover (a backup readiness request's topic set, for instance) still surfaces.
